# the contributor audit: shared original caps and exact flat symmetric rounding

The root independently read both complete arguments and their dependencies,
and ran both companion verifiers. Neither result proves unrestricted OC.

## Shared original cap equations

`candidate 004e194a6aeb29ff` passes.
The augmented continuous circuit matrix is invertible because a positive
dependence first annihilates its last scalar coordinate, and continuous
rank then annihilates the remaining vector. Its raw-margin representation
and criterion F_g(z)>=0 are exact, including zero projected margins.

A shared original has a single normal and a single affine base coefficient.
Subtracting its two representations yields the stated finite equation;
differentiation yields the stacked linear system and its exact cokernel.
Private normals cannot remove a shared identity. The independence of the
t-1 differences follows from affine independence of a full circuit. The
constant-rank finite solvability qualification is needed and included.

The five-cap example has the stated actual exclusive witnesses. Its
coefficient comparison forces a=1 and t=0, while the t-squared path
correctly illustrates failure of a prescribed finite path, not failure of
integrability of the zero tangent. The positive offset repair applies once
to every original and enlarges caps; no favorable mass sign is inferred.

For fixed Q and f, changing one normal in the shared matrix kernel is an
exact physical cap motion preserving all selected groups. The coarea
derivative includes every actual fiber and the varying base coefficients.
Changing the reference section changes the force only by a vector in the
row space. Consequently stationarity under precisely these motions is
equivalent to R belonging to that row space. This is a condition on that
individual cap mass. An application to a multiplier-weighted objective
would additionally need a positive multiplier on this cap; no automatic
such implication is part of the proved lemma. The explicit square example
realizes a nonzero force in the shared row space, with every permitted
motion bisecting both fibers exactly.

Supporting-face traces are excluded from the differentiability statement;
the general boundary case is not silently smoothed away. The defect-one
incidence consequence is conditional on full-rank selected groups, as
stated. The exact verifier passes all witness, rank, repair, and obstruction
checks.

## Symmetric flat rounding and reduced curvature

`candidate 6f9d37b455a5cd1c` passes the
root's proof audit. A separate agent audit is requested.

For each excluded-self representation, the extra support margin is
epsilon times the weighted squared base distance. The minimum lattice
distance gives a uniform margin for all real coefficient representations,
not only their vertices. Removing selfweight is legitimate. Hausdorff
errors cost at most twice their size, giving an actual open family. The
lattice-complete projection and all anchored inclusions imply that its
convex hull has exactly the specified integer fibers.

Reflection preserves every nonvertical through-origin half-mass budget,
including after rounding and a common volume normalization. This is the
entire-source sum; individual unchanged fibers need not have smooth cap
functions. The cancellation in equation (10) is therefore exact and is
the reason only the selected simplex needs regular cap derivatives.

The face-tube regularity proof is valid: nearest-point tubes of distinct
relative face interiors are disjoint up to null sets; their tangent and
normal spaces are orthogonal. A proper canonical cap separates one vertex
uniformly from all others. Thus all sufficiently thin tubes keep the same
facewise sign pattern, and the retained face area is the displayed
simplex power. Under an affine perturbation the normal cone is transformed
by the inverse transpose. Its fixed-domain polar Jacobian is exactly
J_W tau^q |L_W theta|^{-q} r^{q-1}. Expansion produces a finite polynomial
of degree at most d with smooth coefficients and uniform C2 bounds. No
claim of strictly curved boundary is necessary.

The physical right inverse is a right inverse for absolute cap derivatives
after division by the original simplex volume. The archived canonical
calculation supplies zero full first variation and positive reduced
Hessian VQ, with Q=(d-1)(2-1/(d+1))/d. The implicit-function correction
exists on a common parameter neighborhood using the polynomial extension
at epsilon=0. Its reduced second derivative converges to VQ. A possible
nonzero rounded first derivative causes no problem: the sum of the two
opposite increments is positive. For each fixed small epsilon, the chosen
displacement can be arbitrarily smaller than its compatibility margin.
The final tiny negative cap target preserves the strict volume gain by
continuity and surjectivity. Common dilation restores exactly the old
baseline mass and cap budgets and preserves whole-space coverage.

The scope is one selected group and an off-center simplex fiber, d>=2,
on a centrally symmetric source. Zero-volume fibers are removed only from
the measured finite geometry; no convergence to omitted real-base geometry
is asserted. The saturated lattice reduction and transverse thin cube
preserve the actual positive fibers. This is a variation on an OC-safe
source, not a general extremizer exclusion.

The verifier passes exact d=2 critical algebra and the independently
derived planar face-tube formula. Its high-precision active-midpoint test
is supplementary evidence only; the all-dimensional proof uses the face
tubes and implicit-function theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
